quote: So it's a single family home. Is there anybody else on the title but you? Oh, do you already have solar?
stewart_read: The co-owner question is asked but the rep's own sentence trails off into a new question ('Oh, do you already have solar?') before the customer answers it. The customer never confirms or denies a co-owner, and the rep never returns to it.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the existing-solar discovery as higher priority and planned to loop back — but no loop-back occurs anywhere in the transcript.
coaching_implication: Flag as an unresolved verify item: closer should ask about title co-owners directly since Bucky's question was abandoned mid-sentence, not because the customer refused to answer.

quote: I wanted to do something like a a EG four system Okay. Or a or a solar system with, the 48 volt batteries so that I could, expand it later with, you know, non brand specific batteries.
stewart_read: Customer gives the single most useful piece of information in the whole call — the exact product category and his reason for wanting it (brand flexibility) — and the rep moves straight to the utility-company question with no acknowledgment or note-taking cue.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may not have the technical vocabulary to engage with 'EG4' or '48V hybrid' and reasonably chose not to fake competence — that's sound scope discipline, but it doesn't excuse failing to reflect the detail back for the record.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge specificity even when redirecting scope: 'Got it — EG4, 48V hybrid, non-proprietary — I'll make sure the specialist has that exact ask.' Costs nothing and protects the handoff.

quote: Do y'all do, do y'all do the, like, the e g four batteries?
stewart_read: Second time the customer raises the exact same brand-specific ask. Rep's answer ('We have tons of batteries. We have, like, multiple.') is vague to the point of sounding uninformed, though the redirect to a specialist immediately after is the correct scope move.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply doesn't know if Ion carries EG4 and covers with a vague answer rather than admitting the gap transparently.
coaching_implication: Better line available within the schema's own escape hatch: 'That's exactly the kind of build the specialist can confirm — let me flag EG4 specifically so they come prepared.' Transparency plus capture beats a vague deflection.

quote: I mean, I can wait. Do you wanna do that real quick? Because
stewart_read: Customer says the bill isn't easily accessible and would require going upstairs; rep offers to wait live on the phone rather than proposing the faster text/photo-later path immediately. It works out (customer volunteers the text option himself at 03:01), but the rep didn't initiate the efficient path.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: waiting live keeps the appointment-setting moving in one call rather than risking a callback — and it did work, closing in under three minutes.
coaching_implication: Minor efficiency note: rep could open with 'no rush — want to just text me a screenshot after we hang up, or grab it now?' to give the customer the faster option upfront instead of defaulting to 'I can wait.'

quote: And do you want me to text you any details on what I'm looking for?
stewart_read: Customer proactively offers to send more detail unprompted — a strong signal of a motivated, well-informed lead who wants the appointment to go well. This is exactly the moment to reinforce the EG4/48V-hybrid detail that was dropped earlier.
coaching_implication: Rep's response ('I got them what I need, but if you wanna text any other details, it'll always help') is passive given the rep in fact did NOT capture the EG4 detail — coach the rep to say 'actually yes, please send the EG4/hybrid spec you mentioned' rather than implying it's already covered.

quote: Alright. I'll text you after this to remind you. We'll call you tomorrow at 2PM, and it'll be for the battery.
stewart_read: Appointment day/time is locked, but there is no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, no one-hour block statement, and no no-driving/computer instruction — the button-up is thin relative to schema, even though the core day+time mechanics succeeded.
alternative_hypothesis: This is a phone-only battery-consult callback rather than a full design review, so some button-up elements (computer, no-driving) may be less load-bearing — but the verbal handshake is still missing.
coaching_implication: Add the confirmation handshake and expectation-setting even on shorter battery-specific callbacks; it costs 10 seconds and protects show rate.
